A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLog research work. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLog benchmark results and ablations in Section 4, plus timing and model-scaling experiments in Appendices A.5 and A.7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, ablation, timing, and scaling results, including the appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The retrieval-token architecture, contrastive objective, Narration Pair Encoding algorithm, hierarchical indexing, and vocabulary-upgrading pipeline are unchanged. Vocabulary expansion without retraining embeddings is newly emphasized, rather than introduced as a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Ego4D/EgoClip-derived Vidcab data, COIN recognition and forecasting tasks, EgoSchema question answering, and HiREST step captioning. Appendix examples retain the same scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout Tables 1–4 and Appendix A.7, including the generative/retrieval baselines, COIN methods, MVU, LangRepo, LLoVi, LLaVA-OV, and Qwen2-VL-7B.

E3.justification: Sections 3.3–4.4 and Appendices A.1/A.4 retain the same splits, sample counts, metrics, frame sampling, fine-tuning settings, and evaluated model sizes. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The vocabulary-upgrading, hierarchical-indexing, reference-video-count, retrieval-token, and language-model ablations are retained. Appendix timing/scaling analyses and qualitative success and failure cases also match.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without documented repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative outputs are unchanged. For example, Table 3 retains VLog's 70.4% subset and 43.1% full-set EgoSchema accuracy, while Appendix A.7 retains 74.8% accuracy and 6.4-second decoding for VLog with Qwen2.

T1.justification: The task definitions, Equations 1–5, and Appendix A.5 complexity reasoning are retained. The added discussion of vocabulary flexibility introduces no new mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction replaces the claim of the first generative-retrieval framework for video understanding with the first narration vocabulary for VideoLLMs, and elevates expansion without training new embeddings as a contribution. This repositions the same work while retaining its efficiency and reasoning claims.

C2.justification: The introduction and Section 3.1 newly explain that retrieval vocabulary is independent of LLM embedding weights, contrasting its expansion with training required for new LLM vocabulary units. Experimental interpretations and the limitations in Section 5 and Appendix B remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The checkpoint identifiers, hyperparameters, sampling and storage details, vocabulary-construction instructions, upgrading prompts, and stated code-access information are retained. No additional implementation or reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: The same 61 references remain, but the novelty positioning shifts toward narration vocabulary and expansion without embedding training. The introduction makes the contrast with CLIP-based retrieval more explicit using an already cited work.

P1.justification: Selected abstract, introduction, related-work, and architecture passages are rewritten around vocabulary flexibility; the section hierarchy and most prose remain intact. v2 adds a corresponding-author footnote and acknowledgements, but also introduces the unfinished phrase 'resulting xxx speedup'.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 revise token annotations and comparisons, with Figure 2 adding explicit vocabulary-upgrading labels and an expanded caption. Existing tables and appendix figures shift position, while the overall display set and two-column format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Sections 1 and 3.1 and Figure 2 more clearly explain why retrieval permits vocabulary expansion without training new LLM embeddings, improving the rationale for the retained design. This is a modest explanatory gain; the method and evidence are unchanged. The new 'xxx speedup' placeholder weakens polish but does not outweigh that clarification.
